Each offer must consist of the following: A.1. CYBERSECURITY SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT (C-SCRM) Proposal / Quote Instructions (corresponding instructions to the factor below) Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Forms The offeror must include in its offer completed Attachment 1, C-SCRM Questionnaire. To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. 2.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. This capability must allow operators to identify and prioritize interoperability issues and potential workarounds within a single system. • 3.1.3.2 Platform Issue Tracking: The software shall provide a mechanism to record and maintain a history of platform-specific issues (e.g., design, testing, operational) through their entire lifecycle. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. This service is also extended to eligible American citizens residing abroad. C.3 SCOPE The contractor shall provide the Library with new perpetual RealSAM Dialog licenses and technical support for perpetual RealSAM Dialog licenses—new or legacy— in its possession. This support includes the services needed to operate and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production. ip_data_security.text: the cost of services needed to operate and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production. My Talking Books is an Amazon Alexa skill that enables NLS patrons to search the NLS collection, browse the NLS collection, retrieve/manage the patron’s Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. Thi

hall provide the Library with license and technical support. This support shall be provided on an annual basis at a firm-fixed price. This support shall be provided in blocks of 500. This support service must ensure that users with legacy RealSAM Dialog licenses can use the My Talking Books skill in production. The contractor shall provide the Library with a price schedule (Attachment J3 - Pricing Chart.xlsx) for the following scenarios: A. RealSAM Dialog License Support – An annual fee for blocks of 500 perpetual user licenses for the RealSAM dialog engine. This scenario reflects the current state of affairs where the contractor is hosting all required non-GFE services (Auth Proxy, Streaming Servers, Dialog Engine, etc.). B. RealSAM Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host the Auth Proxy service instead of the contractor. C. RealSAM Legacy Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy and Streaming Servers hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host both the Auth Proxy service and Streaming Servers instead of the contractor. Dans le cadre de contrats avec AT, le travail à réaliser peut être défini, mais la nature et les échéances précises des services, des activités et des produits livrables requis ne sont connus qu'au moment où le service est demandé pendant la durée du contrat.
